answer: In an agent market trading ferrous scrap, quartz, and walnut timber, dispute votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, with each token counted only once. Splitting a stake among a thousand fake agents gives the attacker exactly the same voting power as one agent. To control a majority, the attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing the risk that its value falls.
